To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
venture capital financing events are associated with increased growth in the number of startup employees and that this effect increases with the size of the financing round.
VC financing events lead to a significant increase in startup employment and the amount of funding is positively associated with the magnitude of the increase in employment.

venture-capital financing has a significant positive impact on the growth of startups, that this impact increases with the amount of financing received and that growth is a necessary but not sufficient condition for attracting VC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
whether VC financing is a cause or effect of growth in startups, and whether the amount invested in a firm affects its subsequent growth.
how VC financing and employee growth are related, and how this relationship changes over time.
the role of VC as a signal of the growth prospects of startup firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VC does indeed lead to growth, but that growth is not a prerequisite for VC financing.
the presence of venture-capital financing does not lead to the growth of startups.
VC financing is not the cause of startup growth but is a signal that growth is occurring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of VC does indeed signal to investors and employees that the firm will grow.
VC financing does indeed signal growth, but that the signal may be stronger when the company is in need of additional capital.
VC is associated with growth, that VC financing events are associated with growth in the short-term and that growth is associated with increases in valuation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of VC is associated with growth of the firm, but the magnitude of the effect is small.
VC financing is not associated with growth of startups.
VC financing is a significant predictor of employee growth in startup companies.
